title: @Transactional has no effect when the annotated method is called from another method of the same class
errorSample:
org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: 실패한 묶음은 롤백되어야 한다 ==> expected: <0> but was: <2>
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.build(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:158)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertionFailureBuilder.buildAndThrow(AssertionFailureBuilder.java:139)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertEquals.failNotEqual(AssertEquals.java:201)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.AssertEquals.assertEquals(AssertEquals.java:152)
    at app//org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals(Assertions.java:590)
symptom: An exception is thrown part way through a batch, but rows written before it stay in the database (for example an assertion that expected 0 rows finds 2). There is no error about transactions; the rollback simply never happens.
cause: Spring applies @Transactional through a proxy around the bean. A public method that calls a @Transactional method on this bypasses the proxy, so no transaction is started and each JDBC statement autocommits.
fixSummary: Put @Transactional on the method that outside callers invoke (the entry point), or move the transactional method into a separate bean and call it through the injected reference, or wrap the work in a TransactionTemplate. Keep the exception behavior unchanged.
